_doc: Field-wide milestones for the timeline (course-specific events live in each course.json). year < 0 means BC.

milestones.title: Bede's Ecclesiastical History
milestones.detail: Bede finishes his Latin history of the English church and people, naming the Angles, Saxons and Jutes as the settlers of Britain and preserving the story of Cædmon, the first named English poet.

milestones.title: The raid on Lindisfarne
milestones.detail: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records the Viking attack on the monastery of Lindisfarne, the start of the contact that brought hundreds of Norse words, including they, them and their, into English.

milestones.title: The Beowulf manuscript
milestones.detail: Around the year 1000 two scribes copy Beowulf, the longest Old English poem, into the manuscript that is its only surviving source.

milestones.title: The Norman Conquest
milestones.detail: William of Normandy wins at Hastings on 14 October. For three centuries French is the language of the court, law and much of the church, and English borrows thousands of French words.

milestones.title: A royal proclamation in English
milestones.detail: Henry III issues a proclamation supporting the Provisions of Oxford in English as well as French, the first royal document in English since the Conquest.

milestones.title: The Statute of Pleading
milestones.detail: Parliament orders that pleas in the law courts be spoken in English, because French was no longer widely understood.

milestones.title: The Canterbury Tales
milestones.detail: Chaucer begins The Canterbury Tales around 1387, writing in the London English that later became the basis of the standard written language.

milestones.title: Caxton's press at Westminster
milestones.detail: William Caxton sets up the first printing press in England. Printing spreads one written form of English and helps to fix spellings that no longer match the pronunciation.

milestones.title: Tyndale's New Testament
milestones.detail: William Tyndale's English New Testament, printed at Worms, is smuggled into England. Much of its wording survives in the King James Bible.

milestones.title: Wilson's Arte of Rhetorique
milestones.detail: Thomas Wilson mocks 'inkhorn terms', the Latin words that writers were borrowing in large numbers — the start of a long debate about borrowing.

milestones.title: Bullokar's grammar
milestones.detail: William Bullokar's Pamphlet for Grammar is the first grammar of English written in English.

milestones.title: Cawdrey's Table Alphabeticall
milestones.detail: Robert Cawdrey publishes the first monolingual English dictionary, a list of about 2,500 'hard words', mostly borrowings, with short explanations.

milestones.title: The King James Bible
milestones.detail: The Authorised Version of the Bible is published; for three centuries it is the English most people hear read aloud every week.

milestones.title: Shakespeare's First Folio
milestones.detail: Two of Shakespeare's fellow actors publish the first collected edition of his plays, eighteen of which had never been printed before.

milestones.title: Swift's proposal for an academy
milestones.detail: Jonathan Swift's Proposal for Correcting, Improving and Ascertaining the English Tongue asks for an academy to fix the language. None is ever founded.

milestones.title: Johnson's Dictionary
milestones.detail: Samuel Johnson's Dictionary of the English Language defines its words with quotations from writers, setting the model for later dictionaries.

milestones.title: Lowth's grammar
milestones.detail: Robert Lowth's Short Introduction to English Grammar becomes one of the most influential prescriptive grammars of English.

milestones.title: Jones on Sanskrit
milestones.detail: In Calcutta William Jones argues that Sanskrit, Greek and Latin share a common source, the idea that led to the discovery of the Indo-European family to which English belongs.

milestones.title: Walker's pronouncing dictionary
milestones.detail: John Walker's Critical Pronouncing Dictionary records and prescribes the pronunciation of English words, the most popular guide of its kind for a century.

milestones.title: Webster's American Dictionary
milestones.detail: Noah Webster's American Dictionary of the English Language establishes American spellings such as color and center.

milestones.title: Macaulay's Minute on Education
milestones.detail: T. B. Macaulay's minute leads the British government in India to fund education in English, a step in the spread of English as a second language across the empire.

milestones.title: The first fascicle of the OED
milestones.detail: The first part of A New English Dictionary on Historical Principles, covering A–Ant, is published under the editorship of James Murray.

milestones.title: The International Phonetic Association
milestones.detail: Teachers of languages found the association that, from 1888, publishes the International Phonetic Alphabet, the basis of the transcriptions in this atlas.

milestones.title: The Great Vowel Shift named
milestones.detail: Otto Jespersen gives the name 'Great Vowel Shift' to the change in the long vowels of English between about 1400 and 1700.

milestones.title: Jones's English Pronouncing Dictionary
milestones.detail: Daniel Jones's English Pronouncing Dictionary transcribes the pronunciation of southern British English in phonetic symbols.

milestones.title: The OED completed
milestones.detail: The last part of the Oxford English Dictionary appears, seventy years after the Philological Society proposed it.

milestones.title: West's General Service List
milestones.detail: Michael West publishes A General Service List of English Words, about 2,000 headwords chosen for learners, used for decades in graded readers.

milestones.title: Quirk et al.'s Comprehensive Grammar
milestones.detail: Randolph Quirk, Sidney Greenbaum, Geoffrey Leech and Jan Svartvik publish A Comprehensive Grammar of the English Language, a descriptive reference grammar.

milestones.title: The COBUILD dictionary
milestones.detail: The Collins COBUILD English Language Dictionary, edited by John Sinclair, is the first learner's dictionary based on a large corpus of real texts.

milestones.title: The CEFR
milestones.detail: The Council of Europe publishes the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, whose levels A1–C2 this atlas uses.
